newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end lower, shrug off inflation news.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end lower, shrug off inflation news.

text.p: Philippine shares slid at the close on Thursday despite positive news on low May inflation and strong four-month exports, traders said.

"The market just went through the natural course of events. It needed to correct and so despite the inflation news which has been discounted, the index ended lower," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital.
The main index closed lower for the third straight day, down 17.67 points at 2,778.44.
The National Statistics Office (NSO) announced shortly before trading that year-on-year inflation in May fell to a 10-year low of 4.2 percent as against 4.6 percent in April.
The Central Bank also cut overnight rates by two percentage points.

"Despite the positive macroeconomic news, the correction should continue until 2,681 points. We have seen the last of the recent lows and we are just gearing up for another uptrend," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities.
In the broad market, losers beat gainers 80 to 29 with turnover at 2.2 billion pesos, way below the daily average.
Dharmala Securities analyst Lawrence de Leon said investors will soon be positioning ahead of the release of second quarter corporate earnings.
